keynums.label: NBFC Net Debt (2026, vs Rs.23,500 Cr in 2019)
NBFC Wholesale Book (2026, vs Rs.18,000 Cr in 2019)
NBFC Equity (2026, vs Rs.4,300 Cr in 2019)
Total Intrinsic Value of Operating Businesses (FY26)

bull_bear.body:
- Consolidated net debt reduced to Rs.10,430 Cr (down 7% YoY); NBFC net debt cut ~90% from Rs.23,500 Cr (2019) to Rs.2,375 Cr (2026), and NBFC wholesale book wound down ~90% from Rs.18,000 Cr to Rs.1,750 Cr over the same period.
- Intrinsic Value is described as the group's 'compass' for capital allocation - the estimated true worth of each business guides where capital is deployed, with an ambition to compound Intrinsic Value at 15-20% CAGR over the next 5 years.
- Total Intrinsic Value of Operating Businesses rose from Rs.32,300 Cr (FY25) to Rs.37,100 Cr (FY26), +15% YoY (17% CAGR from Mar 21-26); Edelweiss Intrinsic Value (after adding corporate assets, less net corporate debt and minority interest) rose from Rs.27,800 Cr to Rs.32,000 Cr, +15% YoY (15% CAGR from Mar 21-26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Seven-business diversified model under EFSL: Alternative Asset Management (EAAA), Mutual Fund (EAML), Asset Reconstruction (EARC), NBFC (ECLF), Housing Finance (NHFL), General Insurance (ZGIL) and Life Insurance (ELI).
- Narrative frames the group as transformed from a leveraged NBFC into a 'fundamentally different, capital-light Edelweiss' via systematic de-risking, patient compounding and an intentional pivot to capital-light businesses.
- Consolidated PAT (Post MI) growth for FY26 (+37% YoY to Rs.547 Cr) is described as driven mainly by the Asset Management businesses (Alternative AM and Mutual Fund).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Business PAT mix FY26 vs FY25, Rs Cr] Alternative AM 265 vs 230; Mutual Fund 85 vs 53; Asset Reconstruction 350 vs 385; NBFC 14 vs 55; Housing Finance 23 vs 19; General Insurance (57) vs (48); Life Insurance (159) vs (127); Operating Business PAT 520 vs 566; Corporate PAT 161 vs (31); (Less) Minority shareholders' PAT 134 vs 137; EFSL Consolidated PAT (Post MI) 547 vs 399.
- [Exceptional items] FY26 Operating Business PAT includes Rs.143 Cr of exceptional items (ESOP cost, one-time Labour Code impact across businesses, and GST impact in Life Insurance); FY26 Corporate PAT also includes a DTA recognised in Q2FY26 (Sep 25) arising from Ind AS consolidation accounting across Edelweiss entities.
- [Corporate action] ERFL merged with ECLF with effect from September 2025; NBFC figures in the deck include both ECLF and ERFL.
- [Segment CAGRs, Mar 20-Mar 26] Alternative AM Fee Paying AUM +24% CAGR (profit +12x); Mutual Fund Equity AUM +51% CAGR (profit +70x, +103% CAGR); General Insurance Gross Written Premium +42% CAGR (AUM +33% CAGR, premium up 8x); Life Insurance AUM +23% CAGR, Embedded Value +10% CAGR (AUM tripled, EV doubled); Asset Reconstruction cumulative recoveries Rs.66,200 Cr since FY16 (up from Rs.22,600 Cr in Mar 20); Housing Finance disbursements +19-24% CAGR (more than doubled, Mar22-Mar26); NBFC MSME AUM +10% CAGR.

deepdive.thesis: Edelweiss positions itself as a capital-light, diversified financial-services compounder built on seven operating businesses after systematically de-risking its NBFC, with Consolidated PAT up 10x since Mar 20.

open.item: Management expects to sign up one more co-lending partnership on the mortgages space in the current quarter, with the co-lending business meaningfully starting from Q2FY22.
Management expects to add about 1.5 million retail customers across all retail businesses in FY22.
Management does not expect any significant further impairments on the wholesale book and expects positive slippages (impairment releases) from next year (FY22) onwards.
Management guided that FY22 profits will remain muted as the group continues to hold excess liquidity and reinvest in businesses.
Management expects to complete the Edelweiss Wealth Management NCLT demerger and subsequent listing in the next 12 to 15 months.
Management committed to halve the ECL Finance wholesale credit book again over the next two years.
Wholesale real-estate portfolio is profiled 30% at or near OC/completion, 40% to be completed within the next 24 months, and 30% beyond two years.
Company remains committed to the asset-light retail credit model (housing and SME) in partnership with banks, acknowledging FY22 retail credit growth will be slower while the platform is built.
Expensive long-term holdco/group borrowings taken during the crisis are scheduled to start being repaid from 2022 (FY22) through FY23, reducing the liquidity drag.
Mutual Fund business is expected to become significantly profitable (Rs 50-100 crore PAT) from FY25 (2024-2025) onwards.
Management expects the wholesale book to halve over the next two years and almost all of it to come back (be recovered) within four years.
Roughly Rs 3,000 crore of equity embedded in the wholesale book is expected to be released back to the group between FY23 and FY26 for shareholders or reinvestment.
Mutual Fund significant profitability is targeted once AUM crosses Rs 80,000-100,000 crore (from Rs 55,000 crore currently).
Long-term target for Wealth Management revenue mix is broking ~30%, advisory ~30%, and distribution and capital ~20% each.
Given adequate capital and liquidity, management is not actively seeking capital-raising partners for its 100%-owned Asset Management and General Insurance businesses.

wtt.summary: Building track record — 1Q logged, no reconciled verdicts yet.
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and reassuring; management owned the two difficult wholesale/impairment years and framed FY22 as a muted 'bridge' investment year rather than claiming a turnaround already delivered.
